elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly states that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County, New York are designated as the forum.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County, New York are designated as the forum.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the designated New York County state and federal courts is exclusive.
elements.evidence: Although Section 28.2 generally states that those courts have exclusive jurisdiction, it expressly permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief concerning confidential information or intellectual property in another court. The preferred position contains no such exception to exclusivity.

elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any permitted fallback law.

elements.element: The designated forum is the courts of Delaware, the courts of California, or the courts of London, corresponding to the selected fallback law.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates courts in New York County rather than Delaware, California, or London.

result.reason: The redline correctly selects New York law and removes the conflicting Singapore forum, but the surviving temporary-injunctive-relief carveout permits proceedings in other courts and therefore prevents the New York jurisdiction from being unqualifiedly exclusive. No preferred or fallback level is fully satisfied. The redline is not minimally sufficient to reach a complete level because the carveout would also need to be removed or limited to relief sought from the designated New York courts. Unrelated commercial terms are otherwise preserved, and the clause remains internally readable.
